callout.title: Consistency is the contract
callout.before: Follow the tree above. Full rules:

styles.owns: Brand primitives, semantic tokens, the @theme bridge.
never: A literal hex in a component

designSystem.owns: Typed token layer: palette metadata, scales, logo descriptors.

never: Domain words such as account or invoice

domainComponents.owns: Composites for one domain; may know accounts, not fetch them.

layoutComponents.owns: Structural shells: AppShell, Container, Section, Grid, Stack.

libDomain.owns: Logic with no JSX: hooks, reducers, validators, codebooks.

libApi.owns: Generated OpenAPI types and the single browser HTTP client.
never: A handwritten copy of a generated DTO
An inline URL in a screen

localization.owns: Language and value codebooks, plus the translate runtime.
never: A translation call to an external API
A user-visible string outside a message file

routes.owns: URL structure; composes components and reads data only.

serverEndpoints.owns: Neutral .NET endpoint examples and their request/response records.
never: Secrets or business rules in browser code

conventions.heading: How the code is written
conventions.description: Presentation in components, orchestration in routes, rules in src/lib.

semanticTokensOnly.why: A primitive or hex value breaks theming across all surfaces.

noHardcodedCopy.rule: No user-visible string inside a component
noHardcodedCopy.why: Every string is a key, so a new market is a file, not a refactor.

noBusinessLogicInUi.rule: No business logic in routes or components
noBusinessLogicInUi.why: Rules live in src/lib, which keeps them testable and reusable.

singleSourceOfTruth.rule: One source of truth per fact
singleSourceOfTruth.why: Generated OpenAPI types in api/generated, presentation labels beside features, languages in localization source files.

dataFirstMarkupSecond.why: Screens render declared lists, so a new row never edits JSX.

deterministicFormatting.why: Explicit options and UTC keep server and browser output identical.

mechanicalNaming.why: kebab-case files, PascalCase components — the name tells the folder.

accessibilityPartOfDone.why: AA pairings, visible focus rings, 44px targets, no colour-only status.

flowSection.heading: How a screen gets its data
flowSection.description: Two flows: API demo crosses the network, admin panel stays local. Select a step to see its file.

build.title: Build
build.body: Webpack compiles React into static browser files.

shell.title: Serve
shell.body: .NET serves those files and exposes the API from one process.

browser.title: Open
browser.body: The browser loads React; the router changes pages without full reloads.

api.title: Read data
api.body: React calls /api; in development the Webpack server forwards that call to the .NET API on port 5000.

stack.heading: What is in the stack, and why

framework.because: Typed file-based routing in SPA mode.

build.because: Fast HMR; ?raw imports quote real source.

styling.because: CSS-first config; the token layer is the config.

data.because: Cache keys, retries and paging for free.

serverData.because: One host for the API, security, logs and React files.

types.because: Generated types keep React and .NET aligned without manual mapping.

typography.because: Brand fidelity, no third-party font request.

stack.accessibilityNote: Accessibility lives in the base layer — focus rings, AA pairings, 44px targets — so screens inherit it.

read.title: Read path — API demo
read.summary: The screen owns no data; every filter and page is a request parameter.

read-route.label: Route component
read-route.detail: useQuery keyed on page, search, segment and scenario
responsibilities: Holds query parameters as state
Renders loading, empty, error and success states
No filtering logic — the server decides
read-route.handsOff: AccountQuery — page, pageSize, search, segment, status, scenario

read-client.label: Typed client
read-client.detail: accounts-client.ts builds the URL and narrows JSON
responsibilities: The only place that knows the base URL
Serialises the query, throws a typed problem on failure
Imports the shared contract instead of redeclaring types

read-handler.label: .NET endpoint
read-handler.detail: GET /api/public/accounts filters, pages and times itself
responsibilities: Validates the query before touching data
Applies filters, then pages the result
Returns the same envelope and problem shape as .NET
read-handler.handsOff: JSON: { items, page, pageSize, total, tookMs }
read-handler.responsibility: Neutral .NET endpoint examples and their request/response records.

read-source.label: Data source
read-source.detail: Seed set today; EF Core behind ASP.NET Core in production
responsibilities: Supplies rows in the contract's shape only
Swapped for the real service transparently
Business rules live here, never in a component

write.title: Write path — admin panel
write.summary: The screen owns its records; each change is one named reducer action.

write-form.label: Form dialog
write-form.detail: Collects a draft and runs the shared validator
responsibilities: Presentation and field feedback only
Validates with the shared validator
Emits a draft; never mutates the store itself

write-reducer.label: Directory reducer
write-reducer.detail: One explicit action per mutation: create, update, setStatus, delete
responsibilities: The only writer of account state
Actions named by intent, so audit or API calls drop in
Returns derived views; components never recompute
write-reducer.handsOff: Next records array plus derived rows and metrics

write-derived.label: Derived state
write-derived.detail: Filtering, sorting and metrics recompute from records
responsibilities: Memoised selectors keep re-renders cheap
Metrics are computed, never stored
Labels and tones come from account-presentation.ts

write-swap.label: Swap point
write-swap.detail: Replace the hook body with server functions — no screen changes
responsibilities: Each action becomes one server function or endpoint
The hook's return type stays identical
Authorisation and audit belong here, never in the component
write-swap.handsOff: Persisted rows via the ASP.NET Core service

pipeline.heading: Request pipeline
pipeline.description: One read, end to end. Four hops, four files.

screen.title: Screen
screen.body: Calls a hook. Knows no URL.

client.title: Typed client
client.body: The only place a URL exists.

route.title: .NET endpoint
route.body: Validates the request and returns the unified response.

service.title: External service
service.body: Optional; called through one configured HTTP client.

systemMap.heading: The whole system in three parts
systemMap.description: Follow the request from the screen to .NET. Each part has one clear responsibility.

browser.title: 1. React interface
browser.body: Pages, buttons and forms run in the user's browser. React displays data; it does not own server rules or secrets.

host.title: 2. .NET application host
host.body: ASP.NET Core receives API calls, manages cookies and sessions, logs requests, and serves the built React application.

external.title: 3. External services (optional)
external.body: A configured HTTP client is the single place where .NET calls a bank service or another backend.

artifact.title: What is an artifact?
artifact.body: It is the ready-to-deploy output of dotnet publish: the .NET application and the compiled React files together in one folder.

react.meaning: The part a user sees and interacts with in the browser.

dotnet.meaning: The server part that owns security, integration and API behaviour.

api.meaning: A documented doorway through which the browser asks the server for data.

openapi.meaning: A machine-readable API description used to generate matching TypeScript types.

artifact.meaning: A tested build output ready for a server or deployment pipeline.

session.meaning: A secure way for the server to remember an authenticated browser between requests.
